You’ll build and operate production pipelines that our traders rely on daily, learning alongside senior data practitioners and taking on greater ownership as your experience grows.

Here’s what the job entails

You will build, migrate and operate data ingestion pipelines, helping modernise how shared market data reaches our users. Working with senior data modellers and data-quality specialists, you will take responsibility for both the code you deliver and how it runs in production. This gives you hands-on experience of large-scale platform modernisation while developing your engineering skills.

More specifically, your responsibilities include:

• migrating existing data collectors (which fetch market and vendor data from websites, APIs and files) onto our modern data platform via our Python and C# based ingestion framework

• building new pipelines that deliver data both to the lakehouse (Databricks/Delta Lake) and to existing trading data systems

• making pipelines reliable: automated tests, data-quality checks, safe re-runs and the ability to reload historical data

• operating and improving the pipelines you build: monitoring data delivery, investigating failures and fixing recurring problems

• working with data scientists to understand their data requirements and make shared source datasets clean, reproducible and ready for use in forecasting and trading models

• contributing with documented examples and reusable pipeline patterns, helping other teams work with shared data and apply our engineering standards

Meet your team

You will join Data Platform Enablement, the team that makes shared external market data trustworthy, consistent and reusable across Danske Commodities. We build and operate the pipelines that collect and harmonise this data, and establish common engineering methods, modelling principles and quality standards. Working alongside Data Platform Infrastructure, which provides the underlying platform capabilities, we help product teams, analysts and data scientists build on a reliable data foundation.

We are a newly formed team of six experienced data practitioners, growing to eight team members, and our backgrounds are currently within data engineering, data modelling, and data science. We are a hands-on team, where we set standards, but we also build and ship and we invest in growing the people who join us. We always seek to leave systems simpler and better documented than we found them.

But enough about us… over to you!

As you will be owning production pipelines and be expected to drive improvements, we imagine that you enjoy taking responsibility for your work and learning from the knowledge around you. We also picture you as a curious person, who is willing to learn more about the field we work in.

Furthermore, we imagine that you:

• hold a relevant educational background within computer science, software engineering, data science or similar – or equivalent practical experience

• have hands-on experience building data pipelines or data applications in Python, SQL or C#

• have a working knowledge of SQL and relational databases

• are familiar with version control (Git)

• are proficient in English - both written and spoken

Please note that prior knowledge of the energy sector is not required for this role.

We’ll take good care of you

At Danske Commodities, we take great care of our people. Joining us means you’ll get a lot of great perks – including social events, cultural experiences, tasty food and benefits to better your health, your life and your future.

Here are some of the benefits we offer our employees:

Shape your development tailored growth plans, 100+ DC University courses & Harvard Learning access

100+ yearly events from office parties to DC Sports events, CS:GO team, student network & more

Global career paths as part of our parent company, Equinor’s 20,000-strong international network

Flexible work life adjustable hours, part-time options & up to 2 work from home days/week

Fuel Fridays one paid Friday off every month (July and December excluded)

Top-tier parental leave up to 26 weeks paid, pension during leave & post-leave support

Unlimited paid child's sick days because family comes first

Extra time off 5 additional days on top of your 5 weeks

Senior days extra time off if you’re 55+

Attractive package 10% pension, health insurance, bonus scheme & more

Share savings the option to join Equinor’s attractive share programme

Home setup covered paid internet, phone & IT gear

Free tickets & discounts culture, family fun, hotels, restaurants & more

Organic meals light breakfast, lunch, snacks, dinner & take-away

Barista café high-quality coffee, always on us

On-site wellness state-of-the-art gym, physio, chiro and massage therapy

HQ in the heart of Aarhus with stunning views, inspiring architecture and close to public transport

…. and much more

jobs.description:
Landfolk is growing, and we want to make our support across booking channels even better. We’re looking for a Team Manager as a maternity cover for our international Guest & Host Care team, with a particular focus on the external booking channels we work with, including Airbnb, Booking.com, Holidu, HomeToGo and Vrbo.

What excites us about this role

Great support starts with a team that has the confidence, guidance and tools to help. Your day-to-day work will bring together people and operations. You’ll create the conditions for your team to succeed, help your colleagues grow and ensure guests and hosts receive knowledgeable, personal support, with quality at every step.

You’ll work closely with the other Team Managers to set clear priorities, maintain high service standards and build a supportive, motivated team. You’ll also help shape the workflows that make our collaboration with external booking channels work in practice.

You’ll lead by example in support and turn everyday experience, feedback and data into improvements to our processes, tools and collaboration. You’ll have real influence on how we work, in a tech-driven organisation that actively uses data, automation, agents and AI.

What you’ll actually do

You’ll balance daily support, people management and improvements to how the team works.

Your key responsibilities:

• 
Lead and develop your team members through ongoing guidance, monthly one-to-ones and specific, constructive feedback

• 
Ensure helpful, timely support by email, chat and phone, with clear standards for quality and follow-up

• 
Develop support workflows for external booking channels, so the team can confidently navigate both Landfolk’s processes and those of each platform

• 
Help resolve complex guest and host cases, disputes and compensation requests within agreed guidelines

• 
Plan shifts for our student employees and ensure coverage during holidays, sickness and peak season

• 
Take part in recruitment and creating thoughtful onboarding programmes together with your manager and relevant colleagues

• 
Use data and support insights to improve service quality, response times and workflows

• 
Build a supportive, inclusive team culture with room for learning, ownership and honest feedback

The role calls for flexibility and availability to meet the needs of the team and the business, particularly during peak season(s).

About you

You’re motivated by helping both people and operations succeed. You bring structure to a busy day, set clear priorities and stay calm when a situation needs extra care.

You might be a great fit if you:

• 
Have experience in customer service, support, hospitality or a marketplace business, ideally with previous team leadership or people management responsibilities.

• 
Enjoy helping others develop through practical conversations, coaching and feedback.

• 
Can balance high service standards, efficient operations and your team’s well-being.

• 
Take a structured approach to staffing, follow-up and process improvements.

• 
Are comfortable picking up the phone yourself and handling difficult conversations with guests and hosts.

• 
Are curious about our tech-driven organisation and how data, automation and AI can support great service.

• 
Are fluent in written and spoken English. Additional language skills are a plus, but not a requirement.

Experience with external booking platforms is an advantage. What matters most is your ability to learn new systems and turn complex workflows into a straightforward day-to-day experience for the team.

Curious about Landfolk?

At Landfolk, we believe the most memorable holidays happen in homes that are loved and lived in. We’re united by curiosity and driven by a shared purpose of helping people reconnect with nature, culture and the people they love.

Here’s a chance to make your mark on a fast-growing and purpose-driven scaleup with more than 9,000 handpicked holiday homes in Norway, Sweden, Germany, Italy, France, Spain and Denmark.

With us, you’ll:

• 
Learn and grow with more than 100 talented colleagues across tech, commercial, customer care, and creative teams

• 
Be trusted, take ownership and let curiosity guide your work and development

• 
Work in a welcoming, open-minded atmosphere where teamwork and laughs come naturally

• 
Explore how AI can support your work, experiment with your team, and share what you learn

• 
Enjoy flexible working hours, a beautiful office in Aarhus and plenty of moments to come together

• 
Join trips to beautiful holiday homes

Together we’ve already accomplished pretty impressive results, and we’re nowhere near done. Read more about Landfolk

Ready to join us?

Your CV doesn’t have to tick every box. We’re interested in how you think, the questions you ask, and the ideas you’re excited to explore.

Send us your CV and a few words about why you’d like to join the team. Include your answers in a short cover letter and send it along with your CV.

We review applications and interview candidates on a rolling basis, so we encourage you to apply as soon as you’re ready, and no later than 30 November 2026.

A few tips before you apply

We look forward to hearing from you.

Bring your service mindset. Enjoy regular daytime hours.

Do you love making people feel welcome, noticing the little details and making a busy day run smoothly? Perhaps you work in a restaurant, hotel, cabin crew or another service role, and you’re ready for working hours that leave more room for life outside work.

At Adversus, we’re looking for an Office Manager to make our office in the heart of Aarhus a welcoming, enjoyable and well-organised place for more than 70 colleagues.

This is a part-time position of approximately 25–30 hours per week, Monday to Friday, with working hours scheduled between 8:30 am and 3:00 pm.

Your role

You’ll take ownership of the practical details that make everyday office life work. From having fresh coffee ready to creating a welcoming space for colleagues and guests, your work will make a difference people notice and appreciate.

Your responsibilities will include:

• Keeping fridges, coffee, snacks and drinks stocked.

• Receiving, unpacking and distributing deliveries.

• Setting out our individually portioned lunches and tidying up afterwards.

• Keeping coffee machines clean and ready for the next cup.

• Keeping shared spaces, meeting rooms and storage areas tidy and organised.

• Handling cardboard, recycling and returnable bottles and cans.

• Monitoring supplies and helping place orders.

• Taking care of practical tasks as they come up.

There’s room for your ideas, too. Whether it’s baking a cake, making the terrace inviting for summer or decorating for Christmas, you’ll have the freedom to add thoughtful touches that make the office feel special.

This is a hands-on role. You should be comfortable with an active working day, including occasional heavy lifting when receiving deliveries or restocking drinks.

What you bring

You know that great service often means noticing what’s needed before anyone asks.

You might have experience as a waiter, flight attendant, receptionist, barista or in another hospitality or service role. That experience would be a great foundation, but there’s no specific education or office background required.

We’re looking for someone who:

• Enjoys helping people and making them feel welcome.

• Takes initiative and follows things through.

• Notice the details while keeping track of everyday priorities.

• Likes keeping things organised and running smoothly.

• Is happy to roll up their sleeves and handle practical tasks.

• Works independently and takes pride in doing a job well.

• Brings warmth, humour and a friendly attitude to the workplace.

Meet Adversus

Adversus is a Danish SaaS company based in central Aarhus. More than 70 colleagues work across teams including Development, Sales and Customer Success.

Our culture is informal and social, with room for different personalities, a good laugh and people who care about each other. In this role, you’ll get to know colleagues across the entire company and become a familiar part of everyone’s working day.

What we offer

• Regular weekday hours and afternoons free.

• A varied role with responsibility and freedom to organise your day.

• An office in the heart of Aarhus.

• A lunch scheme.

• Health and dental insurance.

• Social events and a friendly Friday atmosphere.

• Colleagues who value what you do.

Interested?

Send us your application and tell us a little about yourself, your service experience and why you’d enjoy taking care of everyday life at Adversus.

We’d love to hear from you.

For more information or questions please contact us at jtr@adversus.io or phone number 60141577

In this Head of Employee Experience role, you'll be…

• 
Setting the vision and one roadmap for our Employee Experience across the employee journey, so colleagues experience one Formalize in every office and every new country.

• 
Building a scalable, intuitive model where people, systems, processes, IT and offices simply work, so day-to-day operations run smoothly on their own, freeing up your team to give personal, high-touch support when it matters most

• 
Setting up one front door for every question on people, workplace and IT, with one ticketing system and a shared knowledge base, solving most questions through self-serve and the rest first time.

• 
Leading a team of around ten across People Operations, Workplace and Internal IT with clear ownership, and making your team's time here a real springboard for their HR careers.

• 
Owning workplace standards, vendors and budgets, and opening new offices on time and on budget from one playbook.

• 
Working with our People Business Partners and Talent Acquisition on journeys that cross teams, such as onboarding and country launches.

Our principle is high touch where it matters, effortless everywhere else, with one front door for every question and the ambition that colleagues hardly need us.

What you bring

• 
Proven leadership experience across the broader employee experience spectrum, combining People Operations with workplace and internal IT, ideally in a scaling international tech company.

• 
A builder's instinct. Your energy comes from systems, standards and support models that work every day. Events and celebrations matter but aren't the core, so if confetti is what drives you, this probably isn't your role.

• 
You think in models, linking the structural basis to the human interaction it enables, and you know where high personal-touch adds value and where good design does the job better.

• 
Strong on digital: people systems, automation and AI are how the team scales, and you're comfortable owning tooling decisions and the budget behind them.

• 
A strong sense of fairness and consistency, with standards explicit enough to guide people rather than slow them down.

• 
A hands-on leader who builds teams across disciplines and grows people into bigger roles.

• 
Clear communication in English, the credibility to partner effectively with our leadership team, and the ability to work from our Copenhagen office (or Aarhus).

What do we offer you?

• 
A monthly salary ranging from 65,000 to 70,000 DKK.

• 
Continuous development through a clear and transparent career framework, so you always know what the next step looks like, with biannual growth talks and regular check-ins.

• 
Thorough pre- and onboarding to set you up for success.

• 
A culture of ownership, trust and independence, with the support you need.

• 
An office-first culture in a central location in Copenhagen or Aarhus, with benefits including pension, lunch, health insurance and social events.

• 
A strong team spirit where we celebrate wins and enjoy time together across offices.

• 
Our annual Global Summit, where the whole company meets and connects.

Our recruitment process

• 
Send your application and upload relevant information

• 
15–30-minute online interview with our Talent Acquisition team

• 
30-minute interview with our Hiring Manager

• 
30-minute interview with our interim Head of Talent Acquisition

• 
Completion of Personality Assessment

• 
In-person team workshop in Aarhus with representatives of People Operations, Workplace and Internal IT, where you work on a real case such as our future onboarding

Would you like to help grow a digital business and bring a traditional industry into the future?

At LeanSails, we're on a mission to make buying new sails easier, more transparent, and more affordable for sailors. We've developed a digital sales platform where boat owners can configure their own sails, explore different options, and get instant pricing online.

Having established our business in Denmark, we're now taking the next exciting step: expanding into Sweden, Finland, and eventually the rest of Europe.

Your role will combine hands-on digital marketing with contributing to our growth strategy as we enter new markets.

Your responsibilities will include:

•

•

You might be a recent graduate or have a few years of professional experience. What matters most to us is your motivation, curiosity, willingness to take responsibility, and ability to turn ideas into action.

Ideally, you:

•

Enjoy working in a small company where ideas can quickly turn into action.

At LeanSails, you won't be managing just one small part of a large marketing department.

You'll join a small, entrepreneurial team where you can work across different areas of digital marketing and see the direct impact of your efforts on the company's development.

We offer:

• 
An exciting position with real responsibility and the opportunity to make a difference.

• 
Hands-on experience with international e-commerce and digital business growth.

• 
An informal working environment with short decision-making processes.

• 
Close collaboration with experienced professionals from the sailmaking industry and business development.

• 
Great opportunities to develop your skills as the company grows.

• 
A workplace in Helsingør, Denmark, with flexibility in your daily work.

Employment Type

We are looking for a permanent employee to join the LeanSails team. This position is therefore not open to freelancers, independent consultants, or marketing agencies.

We welcome applications from both recent graduates and experienced candidates. Our priority is finding the right person who wants to become part of our company and contribute to its long-term development.

About LeanSails

LeanSails is a Danish e-commerce company selling custom-made sails directly to boat owners through an innovative digital platform.

Ready to Join Us?

We look forward to hearing from you!

Postdoc in Nutritional Metabolomics, Department of Nutrition, Exercise and Sports
 Faculty of Science, University of Copenhagen

  Are you interested in metabolomics and its role in advancing nutrition research? Are you good at working independently, but also enjoy being part of an ambitious and collaborating team? Are you driven by challenging the status quo? Then you might be our new postdoc! The position is to be filled by 1 April 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

  This 2-year postdoctoral position addresses latest innovations in biomarker-driven dietary assessment to improve nutrition research with a specific interest in cardiometabolic diseases. The primary tasks are to validate biomarkers for the intake of commonly consumed foods and to utilize them in estimating dietary intake in nutrition studies. For this, the postdoc will work with LC-MS metabolomics profiles of human samples and will develop data-driven frameworks for the implementation of biomarkers of food intake as dietary assessment tools. The position is affiliated with the Foodprints project funded by the Novo Nordisk Foundation.

  Responsibilities and qualifications

  We are looking for a motivated postdoctoral researcher interested in elucidating how an objective dietary assessment contributes to a better understanding of diet-cardiometabolic risk interactions by performing metabolomics analyses and integrating omics with self-reported dietary data from human studies. Additionally, the candidate will be involved in the supervision of the group’s Ph.D., Master and Bachelor students. The work will involve:

   	
• LC-MS data extraction and preprocessing 	
• Integration of diet and metabolomics data through uni- and multivariate statistical analyses 	
• Collaboration with other researchers, technicians and students affiliated with the project 	
• Dissemination of results in the form of conference contributions and scientific publications 	
• Teaching at nutrition and metabolomics courses depending on interests/expertise   The candidate we seek

   	
• Has a PhD degree in metabolomics, chemometrics, bioinformatics or other related areas, ideally applied to human research 	
• Has demonstrated expertise in mass-spectrometric data analyses (e.g. metabolomics) 	
• Has demonstrated expertise in omics data integration and flair for programming (R is an advantage) 	
• Has an excellent publication track record (or equivalent experience) and strong scientific drive 	
• Is motivated by both personal and team accomplishments 	
• Thrives on multidisciplinary collaboration and is curious and open-minded 	
• Has experience and a proven track record of successful collaboration in diverse research environments   As a formal requirement, you must hold a PhD degree (or equivalent). Experience with nutrition research (dietary interventions and/or cohort studies) is an advantage.

  We offer

  The period of employment is 2 years. The expected starting date is 1st of April 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

  You will contribute to the activities of the Nutrition and Biomarkers Group led by Assistant Professor Catalina Cuparencu, which is embeded within the Nutrition, Microbiome and Metabolomics Research Group at Department of Nutrition, Exercise and Sports, Faculty of Science at University of Copenhagen. We offer a dynamic, sociable, collaborative, and international environment with exciting scientific challenges and opportunities to further develop your scientific career. Beyond our expertise in nutrition, microbiome and metabolomics, we offer access to our metabolomics facility and facilities dedicated to cohort- and intervention studies.

  The University is situated in Copenhagen, which is consistently rated among the world's top 10 most livable and sustainable cities. Life for families is made easier via a publicly supported daycare and healthcare system, dual-career opportunities, maternity/parental leave, and six weeks of annual vacation. International candidates may find useful information on living and working in Denmark. Useful information is also available at the university’s International Staff Mobility (ISM) office, which offers a variety of services to international researchers coming to and working at the University of Copenhagen.

  The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.

  Terms of employment

  The position is covered by the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff.

  Terms of appointment and payment accord to the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State.

  Negotiation for salary supplement is possible.

  The application, in English, must be submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below.

  Please include 

   	
• Application (Cover letter) 	
• CV 	
• Diplomas (Master and PhD degree or equivalent) 	
• Complete publication list   
 The deadline for applications is December 13, 2026, 23:59 GMT +1. 

  After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorized recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the Interview Committee. 

  You can read about the recruitment process at http://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/.

  Interviews are expected to be held in January 2027.  

  Further information

  Further information about the position may be obtained from Assistant Professor Catalina Cuparencu, Department of Nutrition, Exercise and Sports, University of Copenhagen (cup@nexs.ku.dk)

PhD Project in Muscular signaling and metabolism

  Nutrition Exercise and Sports (NEXS), Faculty of Science, University of Copenhagen

  The August Krogh Section for Human and Molecular Physiology at Department of Nutrition, Exercise and Sports invites applicants for a PhD fellowship in “Elucidating the role of AMPK in Skeletal Muscular signaling and metabolism”. The project is part of the research project “Illuminating the signaling architecture of skeletal muscle insulin resistance”, which is financed by the Novo Nordisk Foundation

  Start date is (expected to be) 1 March 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

  The project

  By the use of phophosproteomics in human skeletal muscle, we recently discovered a novel phosphorylation site on AMPK alpha2 subunit regulated by mTORC1. This phosphorylation is associate with glucose uptake. We now wish to explore the relationship between the catabolic signal from AMPK and the anabolic signal from mTORC1 and the potential causal link to metabolic regulation. The project will primarily be conducted in mice by the use of transgenic KI models.

  Who are we looking for?

  We welcome applications from candidates with a strong academic background in physiology, biology, biomedical sciences, exercise science or a related field, and an interest in skeletal muscle physiology and metabolic regulation.

  The project combines animal studies with molecular and metabolic analyses. Experience in one or more relevant areas is an advantage, but applicants are not expected to have all of the skills already. Relevant experience could include in vivo or ex vivo research, metabolic phenotyping, muscle physiology, tissue processing, immunoblotting, immunoprecipitation or tracer-based assays.

  An interest in molecular signalling pathways involved in metabolism, including AMPK and nutrient sensing, would be valuable. Above all, we are looking for a curious and motivated researcher who is keen to learn and develop within a collaborative research environment.

  Our group and research- and what do we offer?

  The group is a part of Department of Nutrition, Exercise and Sports at the Faculty of Scince, University of Copenhagen. We are located in Copenhagen.

  We offer creative and stimulating working conditions in dynamic and international research environment. Our research facilities include modern laboratories and animal facilities.

  Our group work focuses on the molecular mechanisms through which physical activity promotes metabolic health.

  We are particularly interested in the intracellular interactions between exercise-induced signaling events and those triggered by insulin, aiming to unravel how a single bout of exercise can enhance muscle insulin sensitivity. Central to these studies is the role of AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) and its interacting partners, including mTOR and TBC1D4.

  We are studying this in humans using various cell/animal models for validation and mechanistic analyses.

  Principal supervisor is Professor Jørgen Wojtaszewski (NEXS, JW@nexs.ku.dk, 45 28751625) and Associate professor Rasmus Kjøbsted (NEXS, Rasmus.Kjobsted@nexs.ku.dk, 45 28344370)

• Complete PhD courses corresponding to approx. 30 ECTS / ½ FTE 	
• Participate in active research environments, including a stay at another research institution, preferably abroad

• Professional qualifications relevant to the PhD project 	
• Diploma allowing independent work with experimental animals 	
• Experiences with experimental animal work 	
• Experiences with experimental animal work related to metabolism and cellular signaling 	
• Experiences with experimental animal work related to skeletal muscle 	
• Curious mind-set with a strong interest in muscle metabolism and cellular signaling 	
• Good English language skills   ***************************************************************************

  Application and Assessment Procedure

   Your application including all attachments must be in English and submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below.

  Please include:

• Original diplomas for Bachelor or Master and transcript of records in the original language, including an authorized English translation if issued in another language than English or Danish. If not completed, a certified/signed copy of a recent transcript of records or a written statement from the institution or supervisor is accepted.

  The Friesen group is looking for a motivated researcher with experience in stem cell biology and metabolism for a postdoctoral position, to commence on January 15, 2027 (or after agreement).

  About us

  The newly established Friesen lab aims to understand, treat and prevent metabolic disease. We want to explore how a cell transitions from a healthy state to insulin resistance to type 2 diabetes and to reverse this process. Our group leverages human pluripotent stem cell (hPSC)-derived in vitro disease models that accurately represent the in vivo cell state. We study the molecular underpinnings of metabolism and insulin signaling in a variety of cell types, improving in vitro hPSC-derived metabolic disease models, and applying these for translational research.

As a founding team member in a new lab, you will have a hand in shaping the lab’s culture and research direction, and you will have early ownership of projects. **Success looks like

• Complex onboarding and implementation projects are managed effectively, with risks identified early and handled proactively

Join us in this role where you’ll help design and develop our new European gas supply–demand modelling capability, supporting short- and medium-term trading and portfolio decisions. You’ll combine strong Python development skills with quantitative modelling and market analysis, working closely with experienced energy market specialists and traders. This is an opportunity to shape the technical foundations of an important new modelling capability and see your work directly influence commercial decisions.

Welcome to Forecasting & Market Analysis You’ll join a collaborative team of quantitative developers and market analysts developing fundamental models, forecasts, and analytical tools across European gas and power markets.

You’ll play a central role in building our European gas modelling capabilities, working alongside colleagues with complementary expertise in energy fundamentals, quantitative modelling, and software development.

As a team, we collaborate across disciplines, share knowledge, and continuously improve how we model and understand energy markets.

You’ll play an important role in:

• co-developing and enhancing our new European gas supply–demand model, supporting gas trading, market analysis, and portfolio management.

• designing scalable, reliable Python-based models and contributing to their architecture, implementation, and continuous improvement.

• modelling fundamental gas market drivers, including pipeline supplies, LNG imports, storage dynamics, consumption, infrastructure constraints, and cross-border flows.

• developing quantitative methodologies to analyse market balances, assess scenarios, and understand short- and medium-term market developments.

• integrating and processing diverse market datasets, ensuring data quality, transparency, and reliable model outputs.

• improving model performance, automation, testing, documentation, and deployment through modern software engineering practices.

• collaborating closely with gas analysts, traders, and other developers to turn complex market questions into practical modelling solutions.

To succeed in the role, you:

• have strong experience in Python development, quantitative modelling, software engineering, or a related field.

• can design and build scalable, maintainable, well-tested quantitative applications and data processing pipelines.

• have a solid understanding of numerical methods, data analysis, time series, or statistical modelling.

• are comfortable working with SQL, version control, automated testing, and collaborative development practices.

• enjoy translating complex real-world problems into robust, practical models.

• are intellectually curious about energy markets and motivated to understand the fundamental drivers behind market behaviour.

• communicate effectively and enjoy collaborating with people from different technical and commercial backgrounds.

It would be an advantage if you also bring:

• experience with European natural gas, LNG, power, or other commodity markets.

• previous experience developing supply–demand, fundamental, forecasting, or scenario models.

• familiarity with European gas market datasets, infrastructure, and price formation.
